companyDescription: Oncology biotech · Gedatolisib pan-PI3K/mTOR inhibitor · FDA Priority Review NDA · PDUFA Jul 17, 2026 for HR+/HER2-/PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer · VIKTORIA-1 mutant cohort doubled PFS vs alpelisib (Jun 2026)
priceNote: 11 days to PDUFA (Jul 17) · up ~677% over 52 weeks — approval optimism largely priced in, but Jul 17 remains a true binary gap event · mutant-cohort data (Jun 2) adds label-expansion optionality not yet in the WT-only NDA
summary: Celcuity's gedatolisib faces an FDA PDUFA decision on July 17, 2026 — 11 days away — for HR+/HER2-/PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer under Priority Review and Real-Time Oncology Review. Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 WT data published in J Clin Oncol showed practice-changing PFS gains; the Jun 2, 2026 PIK3CA-mutant cohort readout doubled median PFS vs alpelisib (11.1 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.50), opening a second regulatory path via sNDA in 2027. The stock has already re-rated ~677% over 52 weeks, so a clean approval may see a muted day-1 gap but a path toward the ~$161 analyst consensus (+79%); a CRL would crash 50%+ overnight. This is a ค่าขนม binary — size 2–3% max, not a trend trade.

catalysts.name: FDA PDUFA Decision — Gedatolisib (PIK3CA Wild-Type ABC)
catalysts.description: FDA target action date for gedatolisib NDA in HR+/HER2-/PIK3CA wild-type advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6 inhibitor + aromatase inhibitor progression. Priority Review, Breakthrough Therapy, Fast Track, and RTOR submission based on Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 WT cohort data.

catalysts.name: VIKTORIA-1 PIK3CA-Mutant Cohort — sNDA Filing
catalysts.description: Jun 2, 2026 detailed data: gedatolisib triplet median PFS 11.1 mo vs 5.6 mo for alpelisib + fulvestrant (HR 0.50, p<0.0001); ORR 48.9% vs 26.0%. Celcuity plans supplemental NDA filing Q3 2026 — regulatory decision expected ~2027, materially expanding addressable population beyond the Jul 17 WT label.

catalysts.name: Commercial Launch — WT Indication
catalysts.description: Company preparing for potential U.S. commercial launch in Q3 2026 if Jul 17 PDUFA clears. First-in-class pan-PI3K/mTOR inhibitor vs single-target alpelisib (Piqray) — launch execution, payer access, and prescriber adoption become the next re-rate driver post-approval.

catalysts.name: VIKTORIA-2 — First-Line Expansion Trial
catalysts.description: Phase 3 trial (n~1,180) evaluating gedatolisib + CDK4/6 inhibitor + fulvestrant as first-line treatment for endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2- ABC. Long-dated pipeline optionality beyond the post-CDK4/6 setting targeted by the Jul 17 NDA.

risks: Heavy pre-PDUFA run-up (~677% over 52 weeks) — even a clean approval risks a "sell the news" fade if the label, pricing, or launch timeline disappoint vs elevated expectations
True binary gap risk on Jul 17 — a Complete Response Letter (CRL) on manufacturing, labeling, or REMS grounds can happen despite strong Phase 3 data and Priority Review
Single lead asset — gedatolisib is essentially the entire investment thesis; no meaningful revenue diversification today

Competitive landscape: Novartis' alpelisib (Piqray) already approved in PIK3CA-mutant HR+/HER2- ABC; AstraZeneca/capivasertib (Truqap) and other PAM-pathway agents compete for the same prescriber wallet
Balance sheet leverage — convertible notes and ~$339M long-term debt (per Mar 2026 filings) mean commercial launch must deliver; dilution or partnership risk if launch stumbles
Mutant-cohort sNDA is a 2027 event — the Jul 17 decision covers WT only; investors pricing full VIKTORIA-1 optionality into the stock ahead of PDUFA face disappointment if WT approval is narrow

macroRisk.rateOutlook: FDA PDUFA decisions are event-driven, not rate-sensitive — the Jul 17 outcome will move CELC independent of Fed policy.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Oncology drug pricing is largely insulated from near-term CPI prints; payer/formulary negotiation and competitive positioning vs alpelisib/capivasertib matter more than macro inflation.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: LOW direct Fed impact on the PDUFA event itself. The broader hawkish-Fed backdrop compresses high-multiple biotech valuations, but a clean Jul 17 approval with a commercially useful label would likely override sector headwinds; a CRL would not get the benefit of the doubt.
macroRisk.summary: Fed risk is LOW for the Jul 17 binary itself — this is a pure regulatory catalyst. Sector-wide biotech multiple compression is a secondary headwind, not the driver of the PDUFA gap.

postWin.note: Travere (TVTX) Filspari FSGS approval (Apr 2026): +33.77% day-1, extending to +46% over 30 days. CELC's massive pre-run makes a muted day-1 (+15-25%) more likely even on approval, with extended drift toward analyst targets ($161, +79%) if launch details impress. Merus (MRUS) Bizengri approval (Dec 2024) rose only +1.8% day-1 — cautionary sell-the-news comp when optimism is pre-priced.

postLose.note: Single-asset biotechs with priced-in approval optimism typically crash 40-60% same day on a CRL, as the market re-rates the entire near-term pipeline toward a much lower approval probability.
